CM2-I1 — Enforce logical dependency depth independently of DFS visitation order. tools/local_validation/cm2/retained.py:130–149 checks the current stack length, but skips dependencies already marked state2. With ordered top-level names m000,m001,..., each depending on its predecessor, every dependency is already finished and the stack remains length1. A chain longer128 is therefore accepted despite the declared depth128 graph limit. Preserve cycle detection, compute dependency height from completed descendants/postorder (or an equivalent order-independent bound), and reject logical height above128. Add boundary/overflow cases in both edge/name directions, including the already-visited-predecessor bypass. Synchronize dependent source/test/registry/roster/inventory pins and bounds.

CM2-I2 — Preserve cleanup FAIL after a body SKIP within the declared negative-cleanup subset. tools/local_validation/cm2/callbacks.py:196–197 permits only ERROR after an existing primary SKIP before cleanup_done. The pinned unittest case.py _addError routes cleanup AssertionError subclasses through addFailure, so SKIP→cleanup FAIL currently refuses before recording that otherwise supported negative callback. This is conservative refusal, not a false accepted run, but it leaves a legitimate cleanup classification inconsistently unsupported. Permit FAIL alongside ERROR specifically in that pre-cleanup SKIP state, retain sticky negative/failfast and all post-cleanup/post-PASS refusals, and add SKIP→FAIL plus mixed/repeated cleanup FAIL/ERROR subcases. State the supported subset precisely in the contract; no runtime semantic-equivalence claim follows.
